fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. Job says, “How then could I gaze with desire at a virgin?” A covenant is a serious promise, and he made this one with his own eyes. It's a promise about where his eyes go.

Not quite, baker. Job asks, “Does He not see my ways and count my every step?” That question treats God as someone who IS watching. Job isn't saying God looks away. He's asking whether God sees his ways and counts his every step.
Right, baker. Job says, “Does He not see my ways and count my every step?” He isn't complaining that God is distracted. He asks whether God sees his ways and counts his every step.

Right, baker. Job says, “If I have walked in falsehood or my foot has rushed to deceit…” and then he names what should happen to him if he did. Verse after verse, he puts a promise behind his claim that he didn't. A man who says that is putting his name behind his innocence.
Right, baker. Job says it's a fire that “…burns down to Abaddon…” and “…would root out my entire harvest.” That's the whole harvest gone. He doesn't treat this as a small thing.
A flock is a fair guess, baker, but it isn't what Job says. The fire in verse 12 “…would root out my entire harvest.” The harvest is what he says it takes.

His friends are a fair guess, friend, but they aren't who Job names here. He says, “…what will I do when God rises to judge?” His worry is about answering to God. Nothing in these verses is about his friends finding out.

True, baker. Job asks, “Did not He who made me in the womb also make them? Did not the same One form us in the womb?” The same One made Job and the servants. Job asks it right after talking about his servants' complaints.

True, baker. Job says, “…from my youth I reared him as would a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided the widow…” That's a long stretch of caring for the fatherless and the widow. Job says it goes back to his youth.

Yes, baker. Job says, “…because I saw that I had support in the gate…” That's the reason he names for lifting his hand against the fatherless. He says he saw support in the gate, and that's the only reason he gives.
Nope, baker, and his friends aren't mentioned here. Job names this reason: “…because I saw that I had support in the gate…” It's about the support he saw in the gate.
Flocks are a fair guess, friend, but here the word is “hand.” He says, “…because my hand had gained so much…” The gain is credited to his own hand.
That's it, baker. Job says, “I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for his life with a curse…” He's saying he did not ask for his enemy's life that way. The word that fits the blank is mouth.
Princes are a fair guess, friend, but Job doesn't name them here. He says, “…my door has been open to the traveler…” The open door is for the stranger who would otherwise lodge on the street.

That's it, baker. Job says, “…if I have devoured its produce without payment or broken the spirit of its tenants…” Taking its produce without payment is the thing he's naming. He puts it in an if, so he's saying he didn't do it.
Thanks is a nice thought, friend, but the word in the verse is “payment.” Job says, “…if I have devoured its produce without payment…” That's the missing piece.
Prayer is a fair guess, baker, but that's not the word in this verse. He says, “…if I have devoured its produce without payment or broken the spirit of its tenants…” The missing word is payment.

Right, baker. Job says, “…then let briers grow instead of wheat and stinkweed instead of barley.” Briers in place of wheat and stinkweed in place of barley is how he ends his list. Then it says the words of Job are done.
